title: Rigveda 5.49: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.49: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.49 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 366v-367v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.49.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 367r
translation.original_text:
1de̱vaṁ vo̍ a̱dya sa̍vi̱tāra̱m eṣe̱ bhaga̍ṁ ca̱ ratna̍ṁ vi̱bhaja̍ntam ā̱yoḥ | ā vā̍ṁ narā purubhujā vavṛtyāṁ di̱ve-di̍ve cid aśvinā sakhī̱yan ||
2prati̍ pra̱yāṇa̱m asu̍rasya vi̱dvān sū̱ktair de̱vaṁ sa̍vi̱tāra̍ṁ duvasya | upa̍ bruvīta̱ nama̍sā vijā̱nañ jyeṣṭha̍ṁ ca̱ ratna̍ṁ vi̱bhaja̍ntam ā̱yoḥ ||
3a̱da̱tra̱yā da̍yate̱ vāryā̍ṇi pū̱ṣā bhago̱ adi̍ti̱r vasta̍ u̱sraḥ | indro̱ viṣṇu̱r varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̱gnir ahā̍ni bha̱drā ja̍nayanta da̱smāḥ ||
translation.text:
1THIS day I bring God Savitar to meet you, and Bhaga who allots the wealth of mortals. You, Aṣvins, Heroes rich in treasures, daily seeking your friendship fain would I turn hither.
2Knowing full well the Asura's time of coming, worship God Savitar with hymns and praises. Let him who rightly knoweth speak with homage to him who dealeth out man's noblest treasure.
3Not for reward doth Pûshan send his blessings, Bhaga, or Aditi: his garb is splendour. May Indra, Visniu, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni produce auspicious days, the Wonder-Workers.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 367r (numbered 40r by the scribe) (OPenn image 367, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.49.1 ‹-bhagam ca ratnam vi-bhajantam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 367v (numbered 40v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.49.4 ‹-vāja-ratnāḥ›. Verses 5.49.1-3 end on this page; 5.49.1 begins on fol. 366v (numbered 39v by the scribe).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.49.4-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 367v
translation.original_text:
4tan no̍ ana̱rvā sa̍vi̱tā varū̍tha̱ṁ tat sindha̍va i̱ṣaya̍nto̱ anu̍ gman | upa̱ yad voce̍ adhva̱rasya̱ hotā̍ rā̱yaḥ syā̍ma̱ pata̍yo̱ vāja̍ratnāḥ ||
5pra ye vasu̍bhya̱ īva̱d ā namo̱ dur ye mi̱tre varu̍ṇe sū̱ktavā̍caḥ | avai̱tv abhva̍ṁ kṛṇu̱tā varī̍yo di̱vaspṛ̍thi̱vyor ava̍sā madema ||
translation.text:
4Sending the shelter which we ask, the foeless Savitar and the Rivers shall approach us. When I, the sacrifice's priest, invite them, may we he lords of wealth and rich possessions.
5They who devote such worship to the Vasus, singing their hymns to Varuṇa and Mitra, Vouchsafe them ample room, far off be danger. Through grace of Heaven and Earth may we be happy.
